newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms after election.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms after election.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate early trading on Monday, gaining increased support after a relatively smooth election last week.
Dealers said there was not much activity on Monday as usual, but forwards weakened on ample liquidity supply in the short-end, with short-term swaps sliding below par.
One dealer in Singapore said capital inflows seemed to have started again in the spot rupiah market after the election.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.5/31.0 at 0300 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.5/32.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,430.85/31.30 and 2,431.1/31.8, respectively.
"The rupiah continues to strengthen regardless of its ample supply. Those are signs of capital inflows," the dealer said.
"We know where the market is heading. Each time we receive a call, we know which side to hit in a quiet market. Rates are drifting to the left," the dealer added.
Economists had expected the rupiah to regain some of its ground if the election proceeded smoothly after sliding in the past few weeks on violent election campaign.
They said the rupiah was backed with sound fundamentals.
Peregrine Securities said there were not enough negatives in Indonesian politics to justify staying out of a market which was supported by robust growth and sound economic management.

However, many dealers remained cautious as the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) will decide on Thursday whether to accept the outcome of last week poll due to what the party claimed of widespread irregularities during the election.
The ruling Golkar swept more than 74 percent of the votes counted, with the PPP taking nearly 23 percent.

Operators were worried of fresh violence and the immediate implication on the rupiah if the PPP declined to sign the election outcome. But for now, dealers seemed to take advantage from the relatively smooth procedure by cashing out from the dollar and increasing rupiah assets.
The Singapore bank dealer said forward rates were still trending down on rupiah over-borrowing established earlier.
"It's still difficutl for forward rates to recover in the short-term because of ample supply in the short-end," he said.
Overnight and tom/next swaps were at -0.30/-0.25 points.
One-month swaps were at 12.25/12.75, two at 24.5/26.0, three at 36.0/37.0 and six at 73.0/76.0 points.
The central bank intervention band on Friday was at 2,416/2,608 and its conversion band at 2,416/2,464.
